docs.text: Driver SFM Flow Meter Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Sensirion SFM digital mass flow meters on I2C: the SFM4300, SFM3003, SFM3013, SFM3019, SFM3119, SFM3304, SFM3505, the legacy SFM3000, SFM3200, SFM3300, SFM3400, SFM4200 and SFM4100, and the preliminary SFM6000D. One API, 32 variants, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves bytes; it does the rest: identification, scaling checks, the command sequences of each protocol family, the CRC of every word, the status checks, the waits and the recovery rules. Not a safety device The vendor states that these sensors are not designed for safety-critical or life-supporting use unless the datasheet says so. This driver is verified against a model of the chip, not against hardware, and carries no medical or safety claim. See Contract . Digital mass flow meters SFM family Sensirion Function Gas mass flow in standard litres per minute (SFM4100: standard cubic centimetres) and the temperature the sensor reports (its silicon; on the SFM3003-300-CET a gas temperature sensor in the flow channel), as signed integers in millilitres per minute and milli-degrees Interface I2C, 100 kHz to 1 MHz depending on the part; no register byte: raw command words and 16-bit words with a CRC-8 Families SF06 (five parts), SF06 gen 2 (SFM3304), SF06 dual (SFM3505), SF05 (five legacy), SF04 (SFM4100), SFx6000 (SFM6000D, preliminary) Integrity CRC-8 on every word, checked before anything is decoded; status word checks; stuck lines are errors Supply 3.0 V to 5.5 V (SFM4300); 3.3 V or 5 V by part, see Hardware What you get ¶ One object for every part. SfmFlowMeter<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until you initialise it. The part is data (a table of 32 rows); the code branches on the protocol family only. See Architecture . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as NoData , Crc , DeviceReset or StateUnknown . See API guide . Non-blocking by construction. Calls that need a wait return it; you sleep, then Poll() . A blocking wrapper exists when the port has DelayUs() . See API guide . Datasheet defaults. PresetFor(variant) gives a valid Config for each part; CheckedConfig proves one valid at build time. See Configuration . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: the bus hooks, plus optional delay, clock, log, clock-stretching read, general call, power cycle and reset pin found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Tested without hardware. Host tests run every part against an independent model of the sensor, a fuzzer checks the driver's promises, and the coverage gate includes MC/DC. See Testing and CI . docs.text: API guide ¶ The driver's API by task, with code that compiles: initialise, measure, update a mixture, run without blocking, sleep and wake, reset, handle errors and shut down. Datasheet sections this page relies on Gen2 start with a filter argument and its status layout: Sensirion AG SFM3304 1.3, Digital interface description (start 0x3603 with filter, status word), p. 11 Dual-gas frame of 24 bits: Sensirion AG SFM3505 D3 1.0, Digital interface description (24-bit frame, commands), p. 10 Sf04 trigger bytes and the hold-master read: Sensirion AG SFM4100 1.4, Digital interface (trigger, clock stretching, address per gas), p. 4 Start measurement, results and the NACK of a read without data: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.1 Start continuous measurement, p. 10 Status word: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.2 Read measurement results, Table 5, p. 11 Concentration update: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.3 Update concentration, p. 11 Stop measurement: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.4 Stop continuous measurement, p. 12 Averaging: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 3.1 Measurement modes; 4.3.5 Configure averaging, p. 12 Scale factor, offset and unit: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.6 Read scale factor, offset and flow unit; 4.5 Unit conversion, p. 13 Soft reset (general call): Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.7 Soft reset, p. 13 Sleep and wake-up: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.8 Entering and exiting sleep mode, p. 14 Product identifier and serial number: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.9 Read product identifier, Table 13, p. 15 Sfx6000 frame, start codes and addresses (preliminary): Sensirion AG SFx6000 I2C 1.1, I2C interface reference (preliminary), p. 6 Legacy command set with pointer registers (Sf05): Sensirion AG SFM-05 not printed (vendor page: 10/2026), I2C functional description (commands, EEPROM, serial, CRC), p. 4 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Lifecycle BeginInitialize() , EnsureInitialized() , Deinitialize() , SoftReset() , HardReset() Measurement StartMeasurement(gas, o2_permille) , ReadSample() , ReadTemperature() , Stop() Setup SetAveraging() , ReadScaling() , UpdateConcentration() Power Sleep() , WakeUp() Waiting Poll() , Poll(elapsed_us) , AwaitPending() , HasPending() State GetState() , GetProductInfo() , GetScaling() , GetStats() , GetConfig() , GetCapabilities() , GetTemperature() Every call that touches the sensor returns a Result : check ok() (or the bool conversion) and read value , or read error . Result is [[nodiscard]] , so an unchecked call is a compiler warning. A call that may need a wait returns Result<Wait> : wait.us is the time you owe the sensor before you call Poll() , and 0 means the operation is done. Which calls a part offers is in GetCapabilities() ; a call the part does not offer returns Unsupported and sends nothing. Initialise ¶ bool Bringup ( Meter & meter ) { const sfm :: Result < void > init = meter . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! init ) { return false ; // NoDevice: nothing answers at the address; DeviceIdMismatch: wrong part } const sfm :: ProductInfo & info = meter . GetProductInfo (); return ! info . prototype && ( info . variant != sfm :: Variant :: Auto ); } The constructor stores the port and the configuration and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start the sensor. It validates the configuration, brings the bus up through the port, wakes or resets the sensor as its family needs, reads the product identifier and matches it to the configured part (the SF05 parts report a serial number, and the SFM4100 has neither), and writes the averaging. Once it has succeeded it returns Ok at once with no traffic, so a handler can call it before every use. After a failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again. Before initialisation every other call returns NotInitialized and sends nothing. GetProductInfo() has the identifier, the serial number and whether it is a prototype or a preliminary part. Read a flow ¶ #include "sfm_flow_meter.hpp" bool ReadOnce ( MyPort & port ) { sfm :: SfmFlowMeter < MyPort > meter ( port , sfm :: PresetFor ( sfm :: Variant :: SFM3003_300_CL )); // no bus traffic yet if ( ! meter . EnsureInitialized ()) { // wakes the sensor, checks the product identifier return false ; } if ( ! meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: Air )) { // reads and checks the scaling, then starts return false ; } if ( ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { // the first sample is ready after the start wait return false ; } const sfm :: Result < sfm :: Sample > s = meter . ReadSample (); if ( ! s ) { return false ; // s.error says why: NoData, Crc, DeviceReset, ... } app :: Report ( s . value . flow_ml_per_min , s . value . temperature_mdegc ); return meter . Stop (). ok () && meter . AwaitPending (). ok (); } StartMeasurement(gas) reads the sensor's scale factor, offset and unit and compares them with the datasheet ( Config::scaling_check ), then starts the measurement. The first sample is ready after the start wait; accurate after the warm-up time ( Sample::settled , which needs NowUs() ). ReadSample() never waits for data: a sensor without a new sample answers the read with a NACK, which is NoData and changes nothing (with an averaging of N a new sample comes every N x 0.5 ms). Only a silence longer than the datasheet bound makes the driver ask with a real command: no answer is NoDevice , an answer is DeviceReset . Without NowUs() the driver never escalates: time the silence yourself and call Stop() , a real command that fails when the sensor is gone. A Sample has the flow in millilitres per minute (rounded to nearest, never clamped), the raw value, the temperature in milli-degrees Celsius where the part has it, the status word and its decoded fields, and a timestamp from NowUs() . The SFM3505 also has the oxygen channel in flow2_ml_per_min . Read the raw words ¶ ReadRawReply() is the single-shot raw access for bring-up and diagnostics: one read of the running measurement that returns the CRC-checked words ( RawReply ) with no decoding, no status check and no range check. GetLastReply() returns the words of the last frame read by either call, without I/O. Use ReadSample() for values: the raw reply skips every check that makes a sample trustworthy. It never reports a silent sensor either: a reset sensor read only through this call returns NoData for ever, and ReadSample() is the call that reports DeviceReset . Update a mixture ¶ On parts with mixtures ( Gas::AirO2 and the others of the table row) the oxygen fraction goes in per mille, from 0 to 1000. UpdateConcentration() changes it while measuring, without a restart: // An SFM4300-20 with 30 percent oxygen in air, then the mixer reports 45 percent. bool Mixture ( Meter & meter ) { if ( ! meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: AirO2 , 300 ) || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; } return meter . UpdateConcentration ( 450 ). ok () && meter . AwaitPending (). ok (); } The sensor needs the two commands of an update back to back, with no read between them; the driver does that. Do not call it more often than once per millisecond. A fraction above 1000 stops the measurement, which is why the driver refuses it with InvalidArgument before sending. Run without blocking ¶ The calls return the wait the sensor needs; the application owns the clock. EnsureInitialized() and the other blocking forms are Begin...() plus AwaitPending() , and need the port's DelayUs() . // The calls return the wait the chip needs; the application owns the clock. A wait of 0 means // "done". sfm :: Result < sfm :: Wait > RunToEnd ( Meter & meter , sfm :: Result < sfm :: Wait > step ) { while ( step && ( step . value . us != 0U )) { app :: Schedule ( step . value . us ); // sleep, or run other tasks, for at least this long step = meter . Poll (); // Poll(elapsed_us) when you keep your own clock } return step ; } bool StartPolled ( Meter & meter ) { return RunToEnd ( meter , meter . BeginInitialize ()). ok () && RunToEnd ( meter , meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: Air )). ok (); } Poll() uses the port's NowUs() ; Poll(elapsed_us) takes the time you waited, and a smaller value than the wait returns the remainder. While an operation is pending every other call returns Busy . For an interrupt-driven design, the SFM4300's IRQn pin is the sensor's own "result ready" line: wire it to an interrupt and call ReadSample() from the handler's task. Handle errors ¶ bool ReadAndHandle ( Meter & meter ) { const sfm :: Result < sfm :: Sample > s = meter . ReadSample (); if ( s ) { app :: Report ( s . value . flow_ml_per_min , s . value . temperature_mdegc ); return true ; } switch ( s . error ) { case sfm :: Error :: NoData : // no new sample yet: ask again later; nothing is wrong break ; case sfm :: Error :: DeviceReset : // the sensor reset under the driver: it is idle, start again ( void ) meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: Air ); break ; case sfm :: Error :: Crc : // a word failed its CRC: the whole transfer was dropped case sfm :: Error :: InvalidReply : // a CRC-valid reply the sensor cannot send: a stuck line app :: Alarm ( sfm :: ToString ( s . error )); break ; case sfm :: Error :: StateUnknown : // a failed command left the mode unknown: initialise again ( void ) meter . EnsureInitialized (); break ; default : break ; } return false ; } Error Meaning Usual action NoData The read was NACKed: no new sample yet Ask again later; it is not a fault DeviceReset No new sample for the whole bound and the sensor then answered a command: the measurement is over and the sensor is idle Start the measurement again NoDevice The address is not acknowledged Check wiring, supply and address Crc A word failed its CRC; the whole transfer was dropped Retry; count it ( GetStats() ) InvalidReply A CRC-valid reply the sensor cannot send (stuck line, reserved value) Treat as a bus fault StatusMismatch The status word does not describe the measurement that was started Stop and start again Stale The sample may not be fresh enough Use or drop it by policy OutOfRange A flow outside the part's span plus margin Check the installation DeviceFault The sensor's scaling differs from the datasheet Do not trust the sensor; see scaling_check StateUnknown A failed command left the sensor's mode unknown EnsureInitialized() again Busy An operation is pending, or the call is illegal in this mode Finish with Poll() All errors with their checks are in Troubleshooting . Sleep and wake ¶ bool NapAndWake ( Meter & meter ) { if ( ! meter . Stop () || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { // sleep is idle-only return false ; } if ( ! meter . Sleep () || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; } // ... the sensor draws the lowest current here ... return meter . WakeUp (). ok () && meter . AwaitPending (). ok (); // the wake polls the address until it answers } Sleep is for the SF06 parts and the SFM3304, idle only. WakeUp() polls with the stop command until the sensor acknowledges it ( Timeout when it stays asleep) and writes the averaging again. SoftReset() while asleep is Busy and sends nothing: a sleeping sensor cannot be soft reset (datasheet 4.3.8); wake it first. The poll that EnsureInitialized() starts with wakes a sleeping sensor too (K-WAKE-INIT). Reset ¶ SoftReset() is the part's reset: the general call 0x06 for the SF06 families, SFM3505 and SFM6000D (it needs Config::allow_general_call_reset and the port's WriteGeneralCall() , because it resets every device on the bus that listens), or a command for the SF05 and SF04 parts. Afterwards the driver is Uninitialized . HardReset() pulses the SFM4200's /RES pin or cycles the supply through the port; without the hook it is Unsupported . A failed reset leaves StateUnknown . The legacy parts count errors in a row ( Config::consecutive_error_limit ); at the limit the driver reports StateUnknown . It does not cycle the supply inside ReadSample() : call HardReset() (the port's PowerCycle() , which must hold SDA and SCL low while the supply is off) and initialise again. Check the scaling ¶ bool CheckScaling ( Meter & meter ) { if ( ! meter . ReadScaling ( sfm :: Gas :: Air ) || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; // DeviceFault: the sensor reports other scaling than the datasheet } const sfm :: ScalingInfo & scaling = meter . GetScaling (); return scaling . matches_table && ( scaling . scale > 0 ); } Shut down ¶ bool Shutdown ( Meter & meter ) { if ( meter . GetState () == sfm :: State :: Measuring ) { if ( ! meter . Stop () || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; } } return meter . Deinitialize () . ok (); // no bus traffic; the next EnsureInitialized() starts from the beginning } Deinitialize() makes no bus traffic: stop the measurement first if one runs. Temperature on the legacy parts ¶ The SF05 parts with a temperature output (SFM3000, the -AW variants and the SFM4200) read it by a pointer sequence that needs 5 ms: ReadTemperature() returns the wait, and GetTemperature() has the value in milli-degrees once the operation ended. A failure after the pointer moved leaves StateUnknown .

docs.text: Group Calls Lifecycle BeginInitialize() , EnsureInitialized() , Deinitialize() , SoftReset() , HardReset() Measurement StartMeasurement(gas, o2_permille) , ReadSample() , ReadTemperature() , Stop() Setup SetAveraging() , ReadScaling() , UpdateConcentration() Power Sleep() , WakeUp() Waiting Poll() , Poll(elapsed_us) , AwaitPending() , HasPending() State GetState() , GetProductInfo() , GetScaling() , GetStats() , GetConfig() , GetCapabilities() , GetTemperature() Every call that touches the sensor returns a Result : check ok() (or the bool conversion) and read value , or read error . Result is [[nodiscard]] , so an unchecked call is a compiler warning. A call that may need a wait returns Result<Wait> : wait.us is the time you owe the sensor before you call Poll() , and 0 means the operation is done. Which calls a part offers is in GetCapabilities() ; a call the part does not offer returns Unsupported and sends nothing.
docs.title: The shape of the API

docs.text: bool Bringup ( Meter & meter ) { const sfm :: Result < void > init = meter . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! init ) { return false ; // NoDevice: nothing answers at the address; DeviceIdMismatch: wrong part } const sfm :: ProductInfo & info = meter . GetProductInfo (); return ! info . prototype && ( info . variant != sfm :: Variant :: Auto ); } The constructor stores the port and the configuration and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start the sensor. It validates the configuration, brings the bus up through the port, wakes or resets the sensor as its family needs, reads the product identifier and matches it to the configured part (the SF05 parts report a serial number, and the SFM4100 has neither), and writes the averaging. Once it has succeeded it returns Ok at once with no traffic, so a handler can call it before every use. After a failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again. Before initialisation every other call returns NotInitialized and sends nothing. GetProductInfo() has the identifier, the serial number and whether it is a prototype or a preliminary part.

docs.text: #include "sfm_flow_meter.hpp" bool ReadOnce ( MyPort & port ) { sfm :: SfmFlowMeter < MyPort > meter ( port , sfm :: PresetFor ( sfm :: Variant :: SFM3003_300_CL )); // no bus traffic yet if ( ! meter . EnsureInitialized ()) { // wakes the sensor, checks the product identifier return false ; } if ( ! meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: Air )) { // reads and checks the scaling, then starts return false ; } if ( ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { // the first sample is ready after the start wait return false ; } const sfm :: Result < sfm :: Sample > s = meter . ReadSample (); if ( ! s ) { return false ; // s.error says why: NoData, Crc, DeviceReset, ... } app :: Report ( s . value . flow_ml_per_min , s . value . temperature_mdegc ); return meter . Stop (). ok () && meter . AwaitPending (). ok (); } StartMeasurement(gas) reads the sensor's scale factor, offset and unit and compares them with the datasheet ( Config::scaling_check ), then starts the measurement. The first sample is ready after the start wait; accurate after the warm-up time ( Sample::settled , which needs NowUs() ). ReadSample() never waits for data: a sensor without a new sample answers the read with a NACK, which is NoData and changes nothing (with an averaging of N a new sample comes every N x 0.5 ms). Only a silence longer than the datasheet bound makes the driver ask with a real command: no answer is NoDevice , an answer is DeviceReset . Without NowUs() the driver never escalates: time the silence yourself and call Stop() , a real command that fails when the sensor is gone. A Sample has the flow in millilitres per minute (rounded to nearest, never clamped), the raw value, the temperature in milli-degrees Celsius where the part has it, the status word and its decoded fields, and a timestamp from NowUs() . The SFM3505 also has the oxygen channel in flow2_ml_per_min .
docs.title: Read a flow

docs.text: ReadRawReply() is the single-shot raw access for bring-up and diagnostics: one read of the running measurement that returns the CRC-checked words ( RawReply ) with no decoding, no status check and no range check. GetLastReply() returns the words of the last frame read by either call, without I/O. Use ReadSample() for values: the raw reply skips every check that makes a sample trustworthy. It never reports a silent sensor either: a reset sensor read only through this call returns NoData for ever, and ReadSample() is the call that reports DeviceReset .
docs.title: Read the raw words

docs.text: On parts with mixtures ( Gas::AirO2 and the others of the table row) the oxygen fraction goes in per mille, from 0 to 1000. UpdateConcentration() changes it while measuring, without a restart: // An SFM4300-20 with 30 percent oxygen in air, then the mixer reports 45 percent. bool Mixture ( Meter & meter ) { if ( ! meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: AirO2 , 300 ) || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; } return meter . UpdateConcentration ( 450 ). ok () && meter . AwaitPending (). ok (); } The sensor needs the two commands of an update back to back, with no read between them; the driver does that. Do not call it more often than once per millisecond. A fraction above 1000 stops the measurement, which is why the driver refuses it with InvalidArgument before sending.
docs.title: Update a mixture

docs.text: The calls return the wait the sensor needs; the application owns the clock. EnsureInitialized() and the other blocking forms are Begin...() plus AwaitPending() , and need the port's DelayUs() . // The calls return the wait the chip needs; the application owns the clock. A wait of 0 means // "done". sfm :: Result < sfm :: Wait > RunToEnd ( Meter & meter , sfm :: Result < sfm :: Wait > step ) { while ( step && ( step . value . us != 0U )) { app :: Schedule ( step . value . us ); // sleep, or run other tasks, for at least this long step = meter . Poll (); // Poll(elapsed_us) when you keep your own clock } return step ; } bool StartPolled ( Meter & meter ) { return RunToEnd ( meter , meter . BeginInitialize ()). ok () && RunToEnd ( meter , meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: Air )). ok (); } Poll() uses the port's NowUs() ; Poll(elapsed_us) takes the time you waited, and a smaller value than the wait returns the remainder. While an operation is pending every other call returns Busy . For an interrupt-driven design, the SFM4300's IRQn pin is the sensor's own "result ready" line: wire it to an interrupt and call ReadSample() from the handler's task.

docs.text: bool ReadAndHandle ( Meter & meter ) { const sfm :: Result < sfm :: Sample > s = meter . ReadSample (); if ( s ) { app :: Report ( s . value . flow_ml_per_min , s . value . temperature_mdegc ); return true ; } switch ( s . error ) { case sfm :: Error :: NoData : // no new sample yet: ask again later; nothing is wrong break ; case sfm :: Error :: DeviceReset : // the sensor reset under the driver: it is idle, start again ( void ) meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: Air ); break ; case sfm :: Error :: Crc : // a word failed its CRC: the whole transfer was dropped case sfm :: Error :: InvalidReply : // a CRC-valid reply the sensor cannot send: a stuck line app :: Alarm ( sfm :: ToString ( s . error )); break ; case sfm :: Error :: StateUnknown : // a failed command left the mode unknown: initialise again ( void ) meter . EnsureInitialized (); break ; default : break ; } return false ; } Error Meaning Usual action NoData The read was NACKed: no new sample yet Ask again later; it is not a fault DeviceReset No new sample for the whole bound and the sensor then answered a command: the measurement is over and the sensor is idle Start the measurement again NoDevice The address is not acknowledged Check wiring, supply and address Crc A word failed its CRC; the whole transfer was dropped Retry; count it ( GetStats() ) InvalidReply A CRC-valid reply the sensor cannot send (stuck line, reserved value) Treat as a bus fault StatusMismatch The status word does not describe the measurement that was started Stop and start again Stale The sample may not be fresh enough Use or drop it by policy OutOfRange A flow outside the part's span plus margin Check the installation DeviceFault The sensor's scaling differs from the datasheet Do not trust the sensor; see scaling_check StateUnknown A failed command left the sensor's mode unknown EnsureInitialized() again Busy An operation is pending, or the call is illegal in this mode Finish with Poll() All errors with their checks are in Troubleshooting .
docs.title: Handle errors

docs.text: bool NapAndWake ( Meter & meter ) { if ( ! meter . Stop () || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { // sleep is idle-only return false ; } if ( ! meter . Sleep () || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; } // ... the sensor draws the lowest current here ... return meter . WakeUp (). ok () && meter . AwaitPending (). ok (); // the wake polls the address until it answers } Sleep is for the SF06 parts and the SFM3304, idle only. WakeUp() polls with the stop command until the sensor acknowledges it ( Timeout when it stays asleep) and writes the averaging again. SoftReset() while asleep is Busy and sends nothing: a sleeping sensor cannot be soft reset (datasheet 4.3.8); wake it first. The poll that EnsureInitialized() starts with wakes a sleeping sensor too (K-WAKE-INIT).
docs.title: Sleep and wake

docs.text: SoftReset() is the part's reset: the general call 0x06 for the SF06 families, SFM3505 and SFM6000D (it needs Config::allow_general_call_reset and the port's WriteGeneralCall() , because it resets every device on the bus that listens), or a command for the SF05 and SF04 parts. Afterwards the driver is Uninitialized . HardReset() pulses the SFM4200's /RES pin or cycles the supply through the port; without the hook it is Unsupported . A failed reset leaves StateUnknown . The legacy parts count errors in a row ( Config::consecutive_error_limit ); at the limit the driver reports StateUnknown . It does not cycle the supply inside ReadSample() : call HardReset() (the port's PowerCycle() , which must hold SDA and SCL low while the supply is off) and initialise again.
docs.title: Reset

docs.text: bool CheckScaling ( Meter & meter ) { if ( ! meter . ReadScaling ( sfm :: Gas :: Air ) || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; // DeviceFault: the sensor reports other scaling than the datasheet } const sfm :: ScalingInfo & scaling = meter . GetScaling (); return scaling . matches_table && ( scaling . scale > 0 ); }
docs.title: Check the scaling

docs.text: bool Shutdown ( Meter & meter ) { if ( meter . GetState () == sfm :: State :: Measuring ) { if ( ! meter . Stop () || ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { return false ; } } return meter . Deinitialize () . ok (); // no bus traffic; the next EnsureInitialized() starts from the beginning } Deinitialize() makes no bus traffic: stop the measurement first if one runs.

docs.text: The SF05 parts with a temperature output (SFM3000, the -AW variants and the SFM4200) read it by a pointer sequence that needs 5 ms: ReadTemperature() returns the wait, and GetTemperature() has the value in milli-degrees once the operation ended. A failure after the pointer moved leaves StateUnknown .

The family mask limits which families an object may drive; a smaller mask lets the compiler drop the rest, and a configuration outside the mask is Unsupported . Family Parts What differs Sf06 SFM4300, SFM3003, -CET, SFM3013, SFM3019, SFM3119 16-bit commands, 9-byte frame (flow, temperature, status), CRC init 0xFF Sf06Gen2 SFM3304 SF06 framing; one gas, optional filter argument, status with the averaging flags Sf06Dual SFM3505 Two 24-bit flows in a frame; no scale read, no status word Sf05 SFM3000, 3200, 3300, 3400, 4200 Pointer registers, EEPROM scale, CRC init 0x00, restart before read, 5 V Sf04 SFM4100 8-bit commands, clock-stretching read, one gas per address Sfx6000 SFM6000D Preliminary vendor protocol, every fact tagged [P] A row of PartInfo holds the product identifier and its mask, the address set, the CRC init, the gas rows (start code, status index, scale, offset, unit), the span, the temperature scaling, the timing, the feature bits, the clock limit and the supply range. The tests type their expectations again by hand from the datasheets and compare them with the table, so a typo in the table fails a test. The executor: plans and steps ¶ A call does not talk to the bus itself. It builds a request, asks the protocol layer for a Plan of at most ten steps, and the executor runs it. The step kinds are Write , Poll , Read , ReadStretch , GeneralCall , Wait , ResetPin and PowerCycle . A Write or a Read is one bus transfer through the port. A Poll repeats the next real command of the family (the stop command, the SF05 serial pointer, the SF04 register read) every millisecond until the sensor acknowledges it or a bound is reached (every loop has a bound). The driver never sends an empty transfer; a NACK on a poll is what a sleeping or resetting sensor answers by design and is not counted as a bus error. A Wait returns control to the caller as a Wait{us} ; nothing in the driver sleeps. The blocking calls are AwaitPending() over DelayUs() . Operations with phases (initialise 2, start 3, read scaling 2, wake 2) build the next plan from the decoded result of the previous one, because what comes next depends on what the sensor said. Every read is a multiple of three bytes. ParseWords() checks the CRC of each word before any value is decoded or stored, and one bad word discards the whole transfer. sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as (measuring) App->>Core: ReadSample() Core->>Port: Read(9 bytes) Note over Core: CRC per word, status check, scale Core-->>App: Result<Sample> State machine ¶ stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Uninitialized Uninitialized --> Idle: EnsureInitialized Idle --> Measuring: StartMeasurement Measuring --> Idle: Stop Idle --> Asleep: Sleep Asleep --> Idle: WakeUp Measuring --> Idle: DeviceReset (silent past the bound) Idle --> Uninitialized: SoftReset, HardReset, Deinitialize Measuring --> Uninitialized: SoftReset, HardReset Idle --> StateUnknown: failed command Measuring --> StateUnknown: failed command StateUnknown --> Idle: EnsureInitialized State Calls that send traffic Refused (nothing sent) Uninitialized BeginInitialize() , EnsureInitialized() , SoftReset() where the part supports it everything else: NotInitialized Idle StartMeasurement() , SetAveraging() , ReadScaling() , Sleep() , SoftReset() , HardReset() ReadSample() , UpdateConcentration() : Busy Measuring ReadSample() , ReadTemperature() , UpdateConcentration() , Stop() , SoftReset() SetAveraging() , ReadScaling() , Sleep() , a second start: Busy Asleep WakeUp() everything else: Busy StateUnknown EnsureInitialized() , SoftReset() , HardReset() everything else: StateUnknown A failed Stop , Sleep , reset, concentration update or the launch phase of a start leaves StateUnknown : the datasheets do not say whether a NACKed command took effect (K-CMDECHO), so the driver does not guess. A failed ReadTemperature() does so only when the pointer moved and was not restored. While an operation is pending (a wait was returned) every other call is Busy ; Poll() continues it. A successful soft or hard reset leaves Uninitialized , because the sensor lost its averaging and its mode. Device-loss detection ¶ A read that finds no new sample is NACKed by design (SFM4300 3.3): the sensor makes a result every N x 0.5 ms for an averaging of N, so with N = 128 a fast loop meets a NACK on most reads. ReadSample() returns NoData for it and changes nothing. Only a silence longer than the datasheet bound decides anything: the time to the first result plus one averaged period (10 % margin) plus 1 ms, measured from the last reply frame the sensor delivered (from the start of the measurement before the first one). A frame counts even when a check rejects it (range, CRC, status) and so does a raw read: a sensor that delivers is not silent. Without a clock the driver never decides: a count of NACKed reads says nothing about time, so the caller times the silence and calls Stop() . After the bound the driver asks with the next real command (the stop command for the SF06 families, the pointer to the serial number for the SF05, never an empty write): no acknowledgement is NoDevice ; an acknowledgement means the sensor is alive and now idle (it was reset, or it has just been told to stop), so the driver goes to Idle , returns DeviceReset and holds the next command for the stop time ( Busy for 0.5 ms). A single transient NACK that arrives after the caller has been away for longer than the bound cannot be told from silence, so it is confirmed the same way (the measurement ends and the caller starts it again). It never restarts the measurement itself, because a restart changes the gas table and the decision is the caller's. The SF05 family also counts errors in a row, because a NACK there can mean a lock-up; at the limit the state is StateUnknown and the caller runs HardReset() , so a read never power cycles on its own. SF04 has no continuous mode and no NoData . Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the I2cPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Optional hooks by requires . DelayUs , NowUs , Log , ReadStretch , WriteGeneralCall , PowerCycle and SetResetPin are detected with C++20 requires . A hook declared with the wrong signature fails the build. Pure plans and decoders. The protocol layer has no state and no port, so it is tested alone and a decoder can run in an interrupt handler on bytes it was given. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state. docs.text: A call does not talk to the bus itself. It builds a request, asks the protocol layer for a Plan of at most ten steps, and the executor runs it. The step kinds are Write , Poll , Read , ReadStretch , GeneralCall , Wait , ResetPin and PowerCycle . A Write or a Read is one bus transfer through the port. A Poll repeats the next real command of the family (the stop command, the SF05 serial pointer, the SF04 register read) every millisecond until the sensor acknowledges it or a bound is reached (every loop has a bound). The driver never sends an empty transfer; a NACK on a poll is what a sleeping or resetting sensor answers by design and is not counted as a bus error. A Wait returns control to the caller as a Wait{us} ; nothing in the driver sleeps. The blocking calls are AwaitPending() over DelayUs() . Operations with phases (initialise 2, start 3, read scaling 2, wake 2) build the next plan from the decoded result of the previous one, because what comes next depends on what the sensor said. Every read is a multiple of three bytes. ParseWords() checks the CRC of each word before any value is decoded or stored, and one bad word discards the whole transfer. sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as SfmFlowMeter<Port> participant Port as Your port App->>Core: StartMeasurement(Air) Core->>Port: Write(read-scale command) Port-->>Core: true Core->>Port: Read(9 bytes: scale, offset, unit + CRC) Port-->>Core: true Note over Core: CRC, compare with the table Core->>Port: Write(start command) Core-->>App: Result<Wait>{12 ms} App->>App: sleep 12 ms App->>Core: Poll() Core-->>App: Result<Wait>{0} (measuring) App->>Core: ReadSample() Core->>Port: Read(9 bytes) Note over Core: CRC per word, status check, scale Core-->>App: Result<Sample>

docs.title: State machine

docs.text: A read that finds no new sample is NACKed by design (SFM4300 3.3): the sensor makes a result every N x 0.5 ms for an averaging of N, so with N = 128 a fast loop meets a NACK on most reads. ReadSample() returns NoData for it and changes nothing. Only a silence longer than the datasheet bound decides anything: the time to the first result plus one averaged period (10 % margin) plus 1 ms, measured from the last reply frame the sensor delivered (from the start of the measurement before the first one). A frame counts even when a check rejects it (range, CRC, status) and so does a raw read: a sensor that delivers is not silent. Without a clock the driver never decides: a count of NACKed reads says nothing about time, so the caller times the silence and calls Stop() . After the bound the driver asks with the next real command (the stop command for the SF06 families, the pointer to the serial number for the SF05, never an empty write): no acknowledgement is NoDevice ; an acknowledgement means the sensor is alive and now idle (it was reset, or it has just been told to stop), so the driver goes to Idle , returns DeviceReset and holds the next command for the stop time ( Busy for 0.5 ms). A single transient NACK that arrives after the caller has been away for longer than the bound cannot be told from silence, so it is confirmed the same way (the measurement ends and the caller starts it again). It never restarts the measurement itself, because a restart changes the gas table and the decision is the caller's. The SF05 family also counts errors in a row, because a NACK there can mean a lock-up; at the limit the state is StateUnknown and the caller runs HardReset() , so a read never power cycles on its own. SF04 has no continuous mode and no NoData .

docs.text: CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the I2cPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Optional hooks by requires . DelayUs , NowUs , Log , ReadStretch , WriteGeneralCall , PowerCycle and SetResetPin are detected with C++20 requires . A hook declared with the wrong signature fails the build. Pure plans and decoders. The protocol layer has no state and no port, so it is tested alone and a decoder can run in an interrupt handler on bytes it was given. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state.

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the SFM flow meter driver promises, what it needs, the rules a caller follows, and what is not verified. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Not a safety device The vendor states that these flow meters are not designed for safety-critical or life-supporting applications unless the datasheet says otherwise. This driver adds no safety claim: it has been verified against a model of the sensor, never against a sensor ( What is not verified ). A design that depends on a flow reading for safety needs its own risk analysis and verification on the real part. Datasheet sections this page relies on Sf04 CRC: Sensirion AG SFM4100 CRC 1.0, CRC calculation, p. 2 Command framing and read framing: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.2 I2C sequences, p. 9 Status word: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.2 Read measurement results, Table 5, p. 11 Stop measurement: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.4 Stop continuous measurement, p. 12 Scale factor, offset and unit: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.6 Read scale factor, offset and flow unit; 4.5 Unit conversion, p. 13 Soft reset (general call): Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.7 Soft reset, p. 13 CRC-8 of every word: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.4 Checksum calculation, Table 14, p. 15 Sfx6000 frame, start codes and addresses (preliminary): Sensirion AG SFx6000 I2C 1.1, I2C interface reference (preliminary), p. 6 Legacy command set with pointer registers (Sf05): Sensirion AG SFM-05 not printed (vendor page: 10/2026), I2C functional description (commands, EEPROM, serial, CRC), p. 4 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. It validates the configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, wakes or resets the sensor as its family needs, reads the product identifier and matches it to the configured part, and writes the averaging. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the sensor returns NotInitialized before initialisation succeeds. No call initialises or resets the sensor as a side effect. Every port failure propagates; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read. Every wait is returned to the caller or bounded; nothing sleeps unless the caller asked for a blocking call and the port has DelayUs() . PresetFor(variant) equals the datasheet configuration of that part. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error only for code that needs it; a misdeclared hook is a compile error. The safety invariants ¶ These are what the tests and the fuzzer check after every call. Id Invariant I1 CRC first. docs.text: The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. It validates the configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, wakes or resets the sensor as its family needs, reads the product identifier and matches it to the configured part, and writes the averaging. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the sensor returns NotInitialized before initialisation succeeds. No call initialises or resets the sensor as a side effect. Every port failure propagates; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read. Every wait is returned to the caller or bounded; nothing sleeps unless the caller asked for a blocking call and the port has DelayUs() . PresetFor(variant) equals the datasheet configuration of that part. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error only for code that needs it; a misdeclared hook is a compile error.

Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Clock 400 kHz typical, 1 MHz maximum for SF06, SFM3304, SFM3505 and SFx6000; 400 kHz for SFM3000/3200/3300/3400; 100 kHz for SFM4200; 120 kHz for SFM4100. 100 kHz ( kSafeClockHz ) suits every part Address 7-bit, no register byte; the sensor accepts raw command words Write START, address + W, command bytes (and an argument word with its CRC-8), STOP Read START, address + R, words of two bytes each followed by a CRC-8, the master NACKs the last byte, STOP Poll A normal write of the next real command (the stop command, the SF05 serial pointer, the SF04 register read), repeated until it is acknowledged; the driver never sends a write with no data byte Repeated START Not used. The documents show a STOP between a command and its read and neither allow nor forbid a repeated START (ambiguity K-RS) The CRC is CRC-8, polynomial 0x31, no reflection, final XOR 0x00; the initial value is 0xFF for the SF06 families and the SFx6000 and 0x00 for SF05 and SF04. A read is always a whole number of three-byte words. The SF05 parts lock up when the master NACKs the first data byte; the port must never abort a read early. SF04 (SFM4100) reads need the sensor to hold SCL low while it measures ("hold master"). The port needs the optional ReadStretch() hook for it, and a controller that does not tolerate a stretching slave cannot run that part. Timing ¶ These are the datasheet maxima the table holds. TimingPolicy::Conservative (the default) waits 20 ms after every SF06 reset and wake; TimingPolicy::Datasheet uses the per-part value and needs a known variant. Family Power-up Soft reset First sample after start Warm-up (accurate) Wake SFM4300 20 ms 20 ms 12 ms 30 ms 20 ms SFM3003, 3013, 3019, 3119 2 ms 2 ms 12 ms 30 ms 16 ms SFM3304, SFM3505 2 ms 2 ms 4 ms 50 ms 2 ms (SFM3505: no sleep) SFM3000 100 ms 80 ms 30 ms 30 ms - SFM3200, 3300, 3400 100 ms 80 ms 100 ms 100 ms - SFM4200 2 ms /RES pulse (unverified width) 100 ms 100 ms - SFM4100 20 ms 20 ms read when ready (stretch) 500 ms - SFM6000D [P] 30 ms 30 ms 12 ms 1 s - After a stop the SF06 parts accept a command within 0.5 ms. The SFM4300 documents 16 ms typical and 20 ms maximum from reset to ready and says the 16 ms holds if SCL is high; the SFM3xxx datasheets say 2 ms for reset but 16 ms typical for a wake from sleep (ambiguity K-TIME). That is why the conservative policy is the default. Under the Datasheet policy a poll gives up a quarter after the figure; Conservative is the supported choice for sleep. Power and reset ¶ General-call reset. The soft reset of the SF06 parts is the byte 0x06 sent to address 0x00. It resets every device on the bus that listens. The driver refuses it unless you set Config::allow_general_call_reset , and the port provides WriteGeneralCall() . A sleeping sensor cannot be soft reset: wake it first. Hardware reset. The SFM4200 has a /RES pin (port hook SetResetPin() ). The other SF05 parts and the SFM3505 reset by cycling their supply (port hook PowerCycle() ). The other parts have no hard reset in the driver: use the soft reset. Without the hook, HardReset() returns Unsupported . Wiring: SDA and SCL must be pulled low at the same time as /RES or while the supply is off (SFM4200 2.3, SFM3505 3.3.5), or the sensor stays powered through the bus lines and does not reset; the port hooks do this and the board must not back-feed the sensor through its pull-ups. See Hard reset wiring . Sleep. The SF06 parts (not the SFM3505) have a sleep mode of about 0.4 µA typical (SFM4300). A wake is a write to the address that the sensor does not acknowledge; the driver repeats the stop command until it is acknowledged. Idle current. 0.055 mA typical, 4.2 mA while measuring (SFM4300, VDD 3.3 V). IRQn. The SFM4300 pulls IRQn low when a result is ready and after a reset until the next start. The driver does not own the pin; use it as an interrupt to call ReadSample() . docs.text: Setting Value Clock 400 kHz typical, 1 MHz maximum for SF06, SFM3304, SFM3505 and SFx6000; 400 kHz for SFM3000/3200/3300/3400; 100 kHz for SFM4200; 120 kHz for SFM4100. 100 kHz ( kSafeClockHz ) suits every part Address 7-bit, no register byte; the sensor accepts raw command words Write START, address + W, command bytes (and an argument word with its CRC-8), STOP Read START, address + R, words of two bytes each followed by a CRC-8, the master NACKs the last byte, STOP Poll A normal write of the next real command (the stop command, the SF05 serial pointer, the SF04 register read), repeated until it is acknowledged; the driver never sends a write with no data byte Repeated START Not used. The documents show a STOP between a command and its read and neither allow nor forbid a repeated START (ambiguity K-RS) The CRC is CRC-8, polynomial 0x31, no reflection, final XOR 0x00; the initial value is 0xFF for the SF06 families and the SFx6000 and 0x00 for SF05 and SF04. A read is always a whole number of three-byte words. The SF05 parts lock up when the master NACKs the first data byte; the port must never abort a read early. SF04 (SFM4100) reads need the sensor to hold SCL low while it measures ("hold master"). The port needs the optional ReadStretch() hook for it, and a controller that does not tolerate a stretching slave cannot run that part.

docs.text: General-call reset. The soft reset of the SF06 parts is the byte 0x06 sent to address 0x00. It resets every device on the bus that listens. The driver refuses it unless you set Config::allow_general_call_reset , and the port provides WriteGeneralCall() . A sleeping sensor cannot be soft reset: wake it first. Hardware reset. The SFM4200 has a /RES pin (port hook SetResetPin() ). The other SF05 parts and the SFM3505 reset by cycling their supply (port hook PowerCycle() ). The other parts have no hard reset in the driver: use the soft reset. Without the hook, HardReset() returns Unsupported . Wiring: SDA and SCL must be pulled low at the same time as /RES or while the supply is off (SFM4200 2.3, SFM3505 3.3.5), or the sensor stays powered through the bus lines and does not reset; the port hooks do this and the board must not back-feed the sensor through its pull-ups. See Hard reset wiring . Sleep. The SF06 parts (not the SFM3505) have a sleep mode of about 0.4 µA typical (SFM4300). A wake is a write to the address that the sensor does not acknowledge; the driver repeats the stop command until it is acknowledged. Idle current. 0.055 mA typical, 4.2 mA while measuring (SFM4300, VDD 3.3 V). IRQn. The SFM4300 pulls IRQn low when a result is ready and after a reset until the next start. The driver does not own the pin; use it as an interrupt to call ReadSample() .

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( sfm_flow_meter_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-sfm-flow-meter.git external/driver-sfm-flow-meter git submodule update --init external/driver-sfm-flow-meter Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-sfm-flow-meter ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE sfm_flow_meter::sfm_flow_meter ) sfm_flow_meter::sfm_flow_meter is an alias of the sfm_flow_meter INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect SFM_FLOW_METER_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver SFM_FLOW_METER_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-sfm-flow-meter -B build-sfm_flow_meter cmake --install build-sfm_flow_meter --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( sfm_flow_meter 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE sfm_flow_meter::sfm_flow_meter ) The target is sfm_flow_meter::sfm_flow_meter in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated sfm_flow_meter_version.h go to include/sfm_flow_meter/inc/ , the template implementation to include/sfm_flow_meter/src/sfm_flow_meter.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-sfm-flow-meter) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-sfm-flow-meter (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-sfm-flow-meter.git components/sfm_flow_meter sfm_flow_meter (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml sfm_flow_meter (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : sfm_flow_meter : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-sfm-flow-meter.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES sfm_flow_meter (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. docs.text: To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-sfm-flow-meter -B build-sfm_flow_meter cmake --install build-sfm_flow_meter --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( sfm_flow_meter 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE sfm_flow_meter::sfm_flow_meter ) The target is sfm_flow_meter::sfm_flow_meter in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . docs.text: Porting ¶ Write the port class for your MCU's SDK. The driver calls hooks on a class you derive from sfm::I2cInterface<YourPort> ; it never calls an SDK. A port is about 20 lines on most platforms. Datasheet sections this page relies on Sf04 trigger bytes and the hold-master read: Sensirion AG SFM4100 1.4, Digital interface (trigger, clock stretching, address per gas), p. 4 Timing (reset, first sample, wake-up, stop): Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 2.4 Timing specification, p. 5 I2C address and bus: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4 Digital interface description; 4.1 I2C address, p. 9 Command framing and read framing: Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.2 I2C sequences, p. 9 Soft reset (general call): Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0, 4.3.7 Soft reset, p. 13 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The contract ¶ The sensors have no register map on the bus. A transaction is a raw command write (a command code, optionally an argument word with its CRC) or a raw read of 16-bit words, each followed by a CRC-8 byte. The port moves bytes; it never retries, never interprets and never aborts a read early. Hook Contract Required bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept Bring the bus up on the first call; true at once afterwards yes bool Write(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) noexcept START, addr + W, len bytes, STOP; false on a NACK or a bus error. len is at least 1: the driver never sends an empty transfer. A NACK is expected while a sensor sleeps or resets (see below) yes bool Read(uint8_t addr, uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) noexcept START, addr + R, len bytes, ACK every byte but the last, STOP; false when the address is NACKed (the "no data yet" signal) or on a bus error yes bool ReadStretch(uint8_t addr, uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) noexcept and static constexpr bool kClockStretch = true A read that tolerates the slave holding SCL low SFM4100 only bool WriteGeneralCall(uint8_t byte) noexcept START, address 0x00 + W, byte , STOP the general-call soft reset of the SF06, SFM3505 and SFM6000D families bool PowerCycle() noexcept Remove and restore the sensor supply, holding SDA and SCL low while it is off (see Hard reset wiring ) optional: HardReset() of the SF05 parts and SFM3505, which the caller runs when the SF05 error limit leaves StateUnknown bool SetResetPin(bool asserted) noexcept Drive the /RES pin of the SFM4200 (active low), holding SDA and SCL low while it is asserted optional void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept Wait at least us microseconds optional: the blocking calls need it uint32_t NowUs() noexcept A free-running microsecond counter optional: settled and staleness checks need it void Log(LogLevel, const char*) noexcept One log line per event; plain text optional addr is the 7-bit address. The hooks are found at compile time: a hook you leave out is not called, and the calls that need it return Unsupported or are refused at build time. A hook you declare with the wrong signature is a compile error that names it. The smallest port: class MyPort : public sfm :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return board :: I2cBegin (); // bring the bus up on the first call; true at once afterwards } bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return board :: I2cWrite ( addr , data , len ); // START, addr+W, len bytes (never 0), STOP } bool Read ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return board :: I2cRead ( addr , data , len ); // START, addr+R, len bytes, NACK on the last, STOP } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { board :: SleepUs ( us ); // optional; without it only the non-blocking calls work } uint32_t NowUs () noexcept { return board :: MicrosNow (); // optional; a free-running microsecond counter } }; A port with every optional hook, for an SFM4100 (the only part that needs a stretching read): class FullPort : public sfm :: I2cInterface < FullPort > { public : static constexpr bool kClockStretch = true ; // marks ReadStretch() for the SFM4100 bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return board :: I2cBegin (); } bool Write ( uint8_t a , const uint8_t * d , std :: size_t n ) noexcept { return board :: I2cWrite ( a , d , n ); } bool Read ( uint8_t a , uint8_t * d , std :: size_t n ) noexcept { return board :: I2cRead ( a , d , n ); } bool ReadStretch ( uint8_t a , uint8_t * d , std :: size_t n ) noexcept { return board :: I2cReadStretching ( a , d , n ); } bool WriteGeneralCall ( uint8_t byte ) noexcept { return board :: I2cGeneralCall ( byte ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { board :: SleepUs ( us ); } uint32_t NowUs () noexcept { return board :: MicrosNow (); } void Log ( sfm :: LogLevel /*level*/ , const char * text ) noexcept { board :: Print ( text ); } }; A port for the legacy parts, which uses the supply and reset hooks: class ResettablePort : public sfm :: I2cInterface < ResettablePort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return board :: I2cBegin (); } bool Write ( uint8_t a , const uint8_t * d , std :: size_t n ) noexcept { return board :: I2cWrite ( a , d , n ); } bool Read ( uint8_t a , uint8_t * d , std :: size_t n ) noexcept { return board :: I2cRead ( a , d , n ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { board :: SleepUs ( us ); } // Both hooks hold SDA and SCL low while the sensor is without supply or in reset, so it is not // powered through the bus pins and really resets (SFM4200 2.3, SFM3505 3.3.5). bool PowerCycle () noexcept { // the legacy parts' last resort: remove and restore the supply board :: BusLow (); board :: SupplyOff (); board :: SleepUs ( 100'000U ); board :: SupplyOn (); board :: BusRelease (); return true ; } bool SetResetPin ( bool asserted ) noexcept { // the /RES pin of the SFM4200, active low if ( asserted ) { board :: BusLow (); // at the same time as /RES, not after it } board :: ResetLine ( asserted ); if ( ! asserted ) { board :: BusRelease (); } return true ; } }; What the bus must do ¶ Requirement Why A write ends with a STOP and a read starts with its own START The documents show a STOP between a command and its read and do not allow or forbid a repeated START (ambiguity K-RS). The driver has no WriteRead hook Never abort a read after the first byte An SF05 sensor locks up when the master NACKs the first data byte; recovery needs a power cycle No empty write, ever A write has at least one data byte. Wake from sleep and every reset poll send the next real command (the stop command, the SF05 serial pointer, the SF04 register read); a sensor that sleeps or resets does not acknowledge its address and the transfer ends there, as an empty probe would have; an awake one accepts the whole command SCL at most kMaxClockHz (1 MHz), 100 kHz when unsure The limits per part are in PartInfo::max_clock_hz and on the Hardware page . Check your setting with static_assert External pull-ups on SDA and SCL The sensors do not have them, and the datasheets give no value. The weak internal pull-ups of a microcontroller do not suit 400 kHz or 1 MHz or the 5 V SF05 parts (the ESP-IDF port leaves them off unless internal_pullup is set, a bench aid only) Clock stretching enabled for the SFM4100 The sensor holds SCL low while it measures sfm::kRepeatedStart is false , sfm::kMaxRead is 18 bytes and sfm::kMaxWrite is 5 bytes: size your buffers and DMA descriptors from them. The clock and the delay ¶ Port has What works DelayUs() EnsureInitialized() , AwaitPending() and every blocking call; the driver loops over DelayUs() NowUs() Poll() measures elapsed time itself; Sample::settled and Config::max_age_us work; Sample::timestamp_us is set neither Only the non-blocking calls: sleep for the wait you were given and call Poll(elapsed_us) Without NowUs() the driver cannot know that a wait ended, so Poll() counts the whole wait as elapsed and settled stays false . Checked at build time ¶ The mistakes a port can make are compile errors, not run-time surprises: Mistake Result The class does not derive from I2cInterface<Self> , or a required hook is missing SfmFlowMeter is not instantiated: the I2cPort concept fails A hook is not noexcept or has another signature The same, naming the hook DelayUs , NowUs , Log , ReadStretch , WriteGeneralCall , PowerCycle or SetResetPin declared with the wrong signature A static_assert names the hook A family mask of 0 or with bits outside the families A static_assert SfmFlowMeter<Port, kFamilySf04> over a port without ReadStretch() A static_assert CheckedConfig built from an invalid Config The build fails, naming ConfigIsInvalid These are tested: tests/compile_fail/ has one case for each, and CTest runs them. Transfers the sensor NACKs by design ¶ These are not bus faults. The driver counts them in Stats::no_data or not at all, never in Stats::bus_errors . Transfer What the datasheet says What the driver does Any write to a sleeping SF06 sensor The address is not acknowledged until the sensor is awake (SFM4300 4.3.8); the address phase wakes it WakeUp() and the identification poll send the stop command every 1 ms up to the part's wake bound; a NACK in between is expected; at the bound the result is Timeout (wake) or NoDevice (initialisation) A write to a sleeping SFM3304 The address is acknowledged, the data bytes are NACKed until it is awake (SFM3304 4.3.8, Table 11) The same poll; the two-byte stop command supplies the data bytes Any transfer after a reset or power-up The sensor does not acknowledge for the reset time (SFM4300 4.3.7) The driver waits the datasheet time, then polls with the next real command A read before a new sample The read header is NACKed (SFM4300 3.3, SFM3003 4.3.1, SFM3505 3.3.1); a result comes every N x 0.5 ms NoData , state unchanged. After the silence bound (first-result time plus one averaged period plus 10 % and 1 ms) the driver asks with the stop command: no answer is NoDevice , an answer is DeviceReset SF05: a read before the first result The read is NACKed (AN-05 4.1) NoData ; the first data byte of a read that is ACKed is never NACKed (lock-up) SFM4200 during /RES Nothing is acknowledged The driver waits the reset time, then polls the serial pointer Control pins: idle levels ¶ A port drives each control output to its inactive level before it enables the output and before the first frame, so configuring it never pulses it. The ESP-IDF port does this in EnsureInitialized() . Pin Inactive level Polarity /RES of the SFM4200 High (released) Active low Supply switch ( PowerCycle() ) High (supply on) Active high; the supply is off only inside PowerCycle() SDA, SCL Released (pulled up) Held low only inside PowerCycle() and while /RES is asserted Hard reset wiring ¶ The SFM4200 datasheet (2.3) says that to interrupt the power to the SF05 chip during the reset, SDA and SCL must be pulled low at the same time as /RES, and the SFM3505 (3.3.5) says all pins, the communication lines included, must be at 0 V for a power reset. A sensor that stays powered through the bus pull-ups or the protection diodes does not reset, so a locked-up SF05 stays locked up. The port's PowerCycle() and SetResetPin(true) therefore hold SDA and SCL low for as long as the supply is off or /RES is asserted, and release them afterwards. On the board, switch the supply of the sensor and its pull-ups together, or make sure the pull-ups cannot back-feed the sensor. The SF05 error limit does not cycle the supply from inside ReadSample() (which never waits): at the limit the state is StateUnknown , and the caller runs HardReset() , then EnsureInitialized() . A port on ESP-IDF ¶ examples/esp32/main/esp32_sfm_flow_meter_port.hpp is a port for ESP-IDF's i2c_master with every optional hook: a stretching read, the general call, a supply switch for PowerCycle() and a /RES pin, both holding SDA and SCL low, and a bus clear after a timed-out transfer. It is compiled by CI and has not been run against a sensor.

Wake from sleep and every reset poll send the next real command (the stop command, the SF05 serial pointer, the SF04 register read); a sensor that sleeps or resets does not acknowledge its address and the transfer ends there, as an empty probe would have; an awake one accepts the whole command SCL at most kMaxClockHz (1 MHz), 100 kHz when unsure The limits per part are in PartInfo::max_clock_hz and on the Hardware page . Check your setting with static_assert External pull-ups on SDA and SCL The sensors do not have them, and the datasheets give no value. The weak internal pull-ups of a microcontroller do not suit 400 kHz or 1 MHz or the 5 V SF05 parts (the ESP-IDF port leaves them off unless internal_pullup is set, a bench aid only) Clock stretching enabled for the SFM4100 The sensor holds SCL low while it measures sfm::kRepeatedStart is false , sfm::kMaxRead is 18 bytes and sfm::kMaxWrite is 5 bytes: size your buffers and DMA descriptors from them.

docs.text: These are not bus faults. The driver counts them in Stats::no_data or not at all, never in Stats::bus_errors . Transfer What the datasheet says What the driver does Any write to a sleeping SF06 sensor The address is not acknowledged until the sensor is awake (SFM4300 4.3.8); the address phase wakes it WakeUp() and the identification poll send the stop command every 1 ms up to the part's wake bound; a NACK in between is expected; at the bound the result is Timeout (wake) or NoDevice (initialisation) A write to a sleeping SFM3304 The address is acknowledged, the data bytes are NACKed until it is awake (SFM3304 4.3.8, Table 11) The same poll; the two-byte stop command supplies the data bytes Any transfer after a reset or power-up The sensor does not acknowledge for the reset time (SFM4300 4.3.7) The driver waits the datasheet time, then polls with the next real command A read before a new sample The read header is NACKed (SFM4300 3.3, SFM3003 4.3.1, SFM3505 3.3.1); a result comes every N x 0.5 ms NoData , state unchanged. After the silence bound (first-result time plus one averaged period plus 10 % and 1 ms) the driver asks with the stop command: no answer is NoDevice , an answer is DeviceReset SF05: a read before the first result The read is NACKed (AN-05 4.1) NoData ; the first data byte of a read that is ACKed is never NACKed (lock-up) SFM4200 during /RES Nothing is acknowledged The driver waits the reset time, then polls the serial pointer

docs.text: A port drives each control output to its inactive level before it enables the output and before the first frame, so configuring it never pulses it. The ESP-IDF port does this in EnsureInitialized() . Pin Inactive level Polarity /RES of the SFM4200 High (released) Active low Supply switch ( PowerCycle() ) High (supply on) Active high; the supply is off only inside PowerCycle() SDA, SCL Released (pulled up) Held low only inside PowerCycle() and while /RES is asserted
docs.title: Control pins: idle levels

docs.text: The SFM4200 datasheet (2.3) says that to interrupt the power to the SF05 chip during the reset, SDA and SCL must be pulled low at the same time as /RES, and the SFM3505 (3.3.5) says all pins, the communication lines included, must be at 0 V for a power reset. A sensor that stays powered through the bus pull-ups or the protection diodes does not reset, so a locked-up SF05 stays locked up. The port's PowerCycle() and SetResetPin(true) therefore hold SDA and SCL low for as long as the supply is off or /RES is asserted, and release them afterwards. On the board, switch the supply of the sensor and its pull-ups together, or make sure the pull-ups cannot back-feed the sensor. The SF05 error limit does not cycle the supply from inside ReadSample() (which never waits): at the limit the state is StateUnknown , and the caller runs HardReset() , then EnsureInitialized() .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ From a bare sensor to a flow reading on your MCU: wire it, write the port, read a sample. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Sensirion AG SFM4300 D1 1.0: Start measurement, results and the NACK of a read without data: 4.3.1 Start continuous measurement, p. 10 Product identifier and serial number: 4.3.9 Read product identifier, Table 13, p. 15 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . 1. Wire it ¶ Every module has a small connector with four to six circuits: supply, ground, SDA and SCL, and on some parts an address pin or a ready line. The pin order of each connector is on the Hardware page . MCU Sensor Notes I2C SDA SDA External pull-up to the bus voltage; the datasheets give no value I2C SCL SCL External pull-up to the bus voltage 3.3 V or 5 V VDD By part: see the supply column of the variant table GND GND Check the supply of your part before you connect it: the SF05 parts (SFM3000, 3200, 3300, 3400, 4200) need 4.75 V to 5.25 V, the SFM4100 3.5 V to 9 V and the SFM6000D 24 V; a sensor on a higher supply needs a bus that tolerates its levels or a level shifter. 2. Write the port ¶ The port is a class with a bus start-up, a write, a read and, for the blocking calls, a delay. The driver never calls an SDK. This is the smallest port that runs an SF06 part: class MyPort : public sfm :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return board :: I2cBegin (); // bring the bus up on the first call; true at once afterwards } bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return board :: I2cWrite ( addr , data , len ); // START, addr+W, len bytes (never 0), STOP } bool Read ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return board :: I2cRead ( addr , data , len ); // START, addr+R, len bytes, NACK on the last, STOP } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { board :: SleepUs ( us ); // optional; without it only the non-blocking calls work } uint32_t NowUs () noexcept { return board :: MicrosNow (); // optional; a free-running microsecond counter } }; Write the hooks with exactly these signatures, noexcept , returning bool : a hook declared any other way does not satisfy the I2cPort concept and the build says which one. Porting has the contract of each hook, including the optional ones. 3. Read a flow ¶ #include "sfm_flow_meter.hpp" bool ReadOnce ( MyPort & port ) { sfm :: SfmFlowMeter < MyPort > meter ( port , sfm :: PresetFor ( sfm :: Variant :: SFM3003_300_CL )); // no bus traffic yet if ( ! meter . EnsureInitialized ()) { // wakes the sensor, checks the product identifier return false ; } if ( ! meter . StartMeasurement ( sfm :: Gas :: Air )) { // reads and checks the scaling, then starts return false ; } if ( ! meter . AwaitPending ()) { // the first sample is ready after the start wait return false ; } const sfm :: Result < sfm :: Sample > s = meter . ReadSample (); if ( ! s ) { return false ; // s.error says why: NoData, Crc, DeviceReset, ... } app :: Report ( s . value . flow_ml_per_min , s . value . temperature_mdegc ); return meter . Stop (). ok () && meter . AwaitPending (). ok (); } What happens, in order: PresetFor() gives the datasheet configuration of the SFM3003-300-CL: its variant and address. The constructor stores it and sends nothing. EnsureInitialized() wakes the sensor, reads the product identifier and checks that it is the configured part. A wrong part is DeviceIdMismatch ; no answer at the address is NoDevice . StartMeasurement(Gas::Air) reads the sensor's scale factor, offset and unit and compares them with the datasheet (a difference is DeviceFault ), then sends the start command and returns the wait until the first sample. AwaitPending() runs that wait with your DelayUs() . Without a delay hook, sleep for the wait yourself and call Poll() ( API guide ). ReadSample() reads one frame, checks the CRC of every word and the status word, and returns the flow in millilitres per minute and the temperature in milli-degrees Celsius. NoData is not a failure: the sensor answers a read with a NACK until a new sample exists. Ask again later. If it does not work ¶ The first line of the answer is the error name. Troubleshooting has a table with the check to make for each one.

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.
